## Purpose

Move the train's root to a promotion flow's first source, or restore the last
cutover. See the [operator procedure](../../guides/git-first-train-runbook.md#moving-the-root-to-a-promotion-flow-source).

## When a playbook uses it

Apply belongs to a local operator. Supervisors can inspect `integration_cutover_plan`
and resolve the blockers with existing integration controls.

## How it works internally

The handler in `src/commands/integration_commands.py` checks local authority.
`src/integration/cutover.py` validates the saved inventory and generation, locks
the project and affected targets, verifies exact Git publication and manual
GitHub settings, then commits the bindings and data fixes through `PolicyActivation`.

## Side effects and persistence

Preview writes nothing. Apply can create missing branches and atomically updates
repository/project defaults, promotion flow, scoped receipt targets and top-level
epic origins. An `integration.cutover` audit record retains prior configuration,
remote policy and exact changed row IDs. The receipt update guard is restored
before commit and checked afterwards. Reverse changes only the audited rows after
the operator restores the recorded workflow list and GitHub settings.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`blocked` includes live root batches and other holders; inspect the plan's named
controls. `stale` requires a fresh configuration generation. Changed saved
inventories require another preview. Named `github_*` refusals identify missing
manual default/ruleset changes or trust mismatches. Failed or unverified branch
publication leaves AQ's configuration untouched; a successfully created branch
can remain after a later refusal.

## Example step

Use the local CLI with a saved plan and its generation:

```bash
aq integration cutover --project demo --flow promotion-flow.yaml \
  --apply --expected-generation 7 --plan cutover.json
```
